limitations: Absence from the inbox does not prove that an event is economically irrelevant.
Materiality channels are assigned by a documented deterministic keyword rule; the semantic novelty of an update is not verified.
Event-family mapping is an optional enrichment; clusters without a mapping show that explicitly.

Event candidates are exact normalized-headline partitions of a stored cluster, so a cross-source paraphrase of one event can appear as separate candidates; conservative splitting is preferred to merging distinct events.
Because event identity is exact, corroboration is counted only when sources publish the same normalized headline; cross-source agreement can therefore be understated.

Lifecycle labels describe candidate timing and workflow age, not economic resolution: RESOLVED means the candidate stopped drawing new articles, and DEVELOPING is not currently produced because a materially different headline becomes a separate candidate.
Why-surfaced names the deterministic inclusion channel rather than a full event-specific assessment, and material-channel coverage is incomplete — corporate earnings and guidance are a known gap.
5 of 6 stored clusters contained more than one identity partition and were surfaced as separate candidates.

non_claim: Events are surfaced through explicit source, identity and economic-channel rules. Inclusion is not a prediction of price direction, significance or tradeability.
